trends.intro: Hair searches rising on Pinterest right now. These are the words clients search with, so using them in captions and on-screen text can help your posts show up when they look.

source.name: Pinterest Trends, US, data through Nov 15, 2026

trends.takeaway: All five are at their highest point of the year right now. Warm, deep tones lead: copper, caramel and cherry brown.

ideas.title: Name the client, then show your order
ideas.principle: Name the kind of client in the first second. Every stylist with that client stops, because now it's for them.
dissection: The hook
The first words on screen are "postpartum bleach and tone tutorial," over the first stroke of lightener. That one word makes you wonder what's different for a postpartum client. That's curiosity.
What they did

About 40 seconds of clean root work, with a 2 to 4 word label for each step. Start at the top, work down the sides, save the hairline for last. Then rinse, tone, and the finished platinum. No talking.
Why people kept watching
Watching neat color go on is satisfying, and each new label makes you want the next step. The finished platinum at the end is the reward.
Why it beat her usual

Identity and practical value. Every stylist with a postpartum client felt it was made for them. The caption explains what she asks, why the hairline goes last, and what she uses. That's why people saved it and sent it. Her other posts show the same service without naming the client, and they get a small slice of the reach.
ideas.concept: Pick a client you handle your own way, like postpartum, first gray, coming off box dye, or a sensitive scalp. Name it on screen. Then film the work you'd do anyway.
ideas.hook: Postpartum bleach and tone: here's my order.
ideas.hook2: First time covering her gray. This is the order I go in.
steps: First frame: put the client type and the service on screen, over your first brush stroke.
Film each step in order. Give each one a 2 to 4 word label, like "hairline last."
End on the finished hair. In the caption, say what you ask this client and what you change.

ref.headline: Postpartum bleach and tone
ref.desc: A platinum stylist put the client type on screen, then showed her root work step by step with short labels. About 45 seconds. No talking.
ref.numbers: About 700K views · about 20K likes · about 11 times the likes of another post of hers

shots: Close on the roots, brush in frame, client's face out of frame
Each section from the same angle, so the labels do the work
The finished hair combed out, back view
structure: Steps in order, one short label each (3–35s)
talking: No voiceover needed. The labels carry it
If you talk, say why you do each step, not just what you do
Put the real expertise in the caption: what you ask, what you change, and why
guide.caption: The client type and service, then 2 or 3 lines on what's different for this client and why. End with: "Save this for your next one."
adapt: Blonding: "first time going blonde over box dye"
Gray: "first gray blend on a client who's always covered"
Cutting: "cutting fine hair that's thinning after illness"
Extensions: "first row on a client with a sensitive scalp"

ideas.title: Their fear, your promise, then cut
ideas.principle: Let the client say what she's scared of. Say your promise back. Then cut straight to the result. The bigger the fear, the more people need to see how it ends.
dissection: The hook
In the consult, the client says how sad she feels when her hair goes back to gray. You hear it in her own words. You feel it with her right away.
What they did
The stylist answers with one line: she'll give her the most modern, natural gray blend. Then a hard cut to the finished hair, a smooth gray-brown bob. The client says "oh my God."
Why people kept watching
Anticipation. The fear and the promise make you need to know if it worked. The hard cut is the surprise. Then her real, happy reaction keeps you there.
Why it worked
It's real. Nothing is staged, and the reaction is hers. A second stylist used the same pattern with a big haircut and also did well. Two stylists, two services, same result.
ideas.concept: When a client has a real worry, like going gray, losing length, or going lighter, film her saying it. Say your plan back in one line. Skip the process and cut to her seeing the result.
ideas.hook: The client's own words about her worry, in the first 3 seconds.
ideas.hook2: "Don't make me look old." Okay. Watch.
steps: In the consult, film 10 to 15 seconds: her worry, then your plan in one line.
Skip the process. Hard-cut to her seeing the finished hair.
Keep her real reaction. Stop once the moment is over.

ref.headline: The gray she was afraid of
ref.desc: A colorist opened on the client's own words about dreading her gray, promised a modern blend, and cut straight to the reveal.

shots: Consult: you and the client at the mirror, phone propped at eye level
Reveal: her face as she first sees it, same spot if you can
Optional: one close shot of the finished hair
structure: Hard cut to the reveal and reaction (15s on)
talking: Let her say the worry. Don't say it for her
Your promise is one sentence, said kindly
Don't coach the reaction. Real beats big
guide.caption: Her worry in one line, your promise, and how she felt after.
adapt: Gray blending: "I don't want to look old"
Cutting: "I'm scared to lose my length"
Blonding: "last time I went blonde it turned orange"
Extensions: "I don't want them to look fake"

ideas.title: Start where it ends
ideas.principle: Show the finished look first. Then show how you got there. End on the same shot so the video loops and people watch it again.
dissection: The hook
The stylist stands behind the client and shows off soft beach waves with her hands. No words. You see the goal, so you want to know how to get it.
What they did
Then a jump to flat, straight hair and a big curling iron. About 38 seconds of every section going around the iron, filmed from the front, so you see the waves build.
Why people kept watching
Watching each wave appear is satisfying, and it's useful. You can learn it. Anticipation: you know what it should look like, and you watch it come together.
Why it beat her usual
It ends on the exact opening shot, so it loops right back to the start. People watch it a second time without noticing. About 4 times the likes of another post of hers.
ideas.concept: Take any blowout, wave, or finish you do at the end of a service. Film the finished look first, then the styling, then the finished look again.
ideas.hook: The finished hair, shown off, in the first 2 seconds. No words needed.
ideas.hook2: This is the wave everyone asks for. Here's every section.
steps: Film the finished look first. Stand behind the client and show it off with your hands.
Film the styling from the front, one section at a time.
End on the same shot as the start, so it loops.

ref.headline: The looping beach wave
ref.desc: A stylist showed off finished waves, then filmed every section around the iron, and ended back where she started. About 45 seconds.
ref.numbers: About 60K views · about 2K likes · about 4 times the likes of another post of hers

shots: Finished look, you behind the client, same spot and light for the start and end
Front view of the styling, phone propped at chest height
Exact repeat of the opening framing
talking: If you add text, keep it to the tool and size, like "1.25 inch iron"
guide.caption: The tool, the size, and one tip that makes it last. Ask: "Want the products?"
adapt: Blowouts: a round-brush finish
Curly: defining curls section by section
Cutting: the finished cut, the cut, the finished cut
Extensions: the blend, start and end

ideas.title: Your most satisfying step, up close
ideas.principle: A step you do a hundred times a day is new to someone who has never seen it. Get close and let the real sound do the work.
dissection: The hook
The first frame is already the step, so close it fills the screen. Hair pulled through a bead, the bead slides up, and the pliers clamp it. No words, no music, just the sound.
What they did
One extension bead, start to finish. 10 seconds. The caption is two words: "Weft asmr."
Why people kept watching
Satisfying. Every move is clean and finishes something, so your eyes want the next one. Curiosity: most people have never seen how extensions go in.
Why it beat her usual
It's so short that people watch it twice, which tells Instagram to show it to more people. About 280K views, far above another post of hers.
ideas.concept: Pick the one step you do over and over that looks tidy up close: folding a foil, a clean section, a bead, a scissor-over-comb pass. Film it so close it fills the screen.
ideas.hook: The step already happening, up close, in the first frame. No words needed.
steps: Prop your phone 4 to 6 inches from your hands. Film one full repeat of the step.
Keep the real sound. No music.
Trim it to under 12 seconds. Caption: "[your step] asmr."

ref.headline: Weft ASMR
ref.desc: An extension stylist filmed one bead going in, so close it filled the screen. 10 seconds. No talking.
ref.numbers: About 280K views · about 20 times the likes of another post of hers

shots: One close shot, hands only, phone propped on a stand
Good light on your hands. A window or ring light
structure: Cut right as it finishes, so it loops
talking: No talking. The sound is the point
Turn off music in the salon while you film
guide.caption: "[Your step] asmr" and nothing more. Short captions fit short videos.
adapt: Blonding: one foil folded and placed
Cutting: one scissor-over-comb pass
Extensions: one bead or tape tab
Color: toner going on at the bowl

ideas.title: Name the shade, then show it
ideas.principle: Give the color a name clients would search for, and put it on screen. A name turns a nice color into something people want to ask for.
dissection: The hook
Color going on at the bowl, filmed from above, with "Dark cherry RED" on screen. The name tells you what's coming, so you wait to see it. That's curiosity.
What they did
4 seconds of thick color going on. Then a jump to the finished hair from the back: deep cherry waves. 8 seconds total.
Why people kept watching
Thick color going on is satisfying. The jump to the finished hair is the reward. The caption adds a surprise: the client came in blonde.
Why it beat her usual

Shade names are exactly what clients type into Pinterest (see What clients are searching below). The name matches what people already look for, so it reached them. About 13 times the likes of another post by the same stylist.
ideas.concept: Name the color you did today the way a client would search for it, like "teddy bear bronde," "butter blonde," or "cherry cola." Show it going on, then the finished hair.
ideas.hook: The shade name on screen in the first second, over the color going on.
ideas.hook2: She came in blonde. This is cherry cola.
steps: At the bowl, film 4 seconds of color going on, from above. Put the shade name on screen.
Jump to the finished hair from the back, with a little movement. 4 seconds.
Caption: where the client started, and the shade name again.

ref.headline: Dark cherry red
ref.desc: A colorist put the shade name on screen while the color went on, then jumped to the finished hair. 8 seconds.
ref.numbers: About 55K views · about 2K likes · about 13 times the likes of another post by the same stylist

shots: From above at the bowl, gloved hands, color going on
Finished hair from the back, in daylight, with movement
talking: No talking needed. The name does the work
Use the words clients search, not formula numbers
guide.caption: The shade name, where she started, and one line on upkeep. Use the shade name a client would type.
adapt: Brunette: "caramel balayage" or "grey blending brunette"
Blonding: "creamy blonde" or "champagne blonde"
Red: "deep cherry brown" or "oxidized copper"
Gray: "gray blending for dark hair"

ideas.title: Clients like this
ideas.principle: Show the trust between you and your client, then the moment she sees her hair. People watch for the real reaction.
dissection: The hook
The stylist round-brushes a client's long blonde while they chat, with "clients like this >" on screen. Every stylist knows the kind of client that means.
What they did
A hard cut to the client in big blonde waves. She says "wow" and touches her hair. A small "before" photo pops up: her 8-month grow-out. Then real chatter: "I just let you do what you want."
Why people kept watching
Anticipation. The blowout makes you wait for the finish. Surprise: the hard cut. Real: her reaction isn't staged.
Why it worked
Identity. Stylists want clients who trust them like this, and clients picture themselves in the chair. About 14 times the likes of another post of hers.
ideas.concept: Next time a client says "do what you want," film the blowout and the moment she first sees her hair.
ideas.hook: "clients like this >" on screen over the blowout.
ideas.hook2: She said "do whatever you want." So I did.
steps: Prop your phone facing the client during the blowout. Text: "clients like this >."
Hard-cut to her seeing the finished hair. Keep her real reaction.
Pop in a small "before" photo with how long it had been.

ref.headline: Clients like this
ref.desc: A blonde stylist filmed the blowout with "clients like this >" on screen, then cut to the client seeing her hair for the first time.
ref.numbers: About 50K views · about 14 times the likes of another post of hers

shots: Phone propped facing the client during the blowout
Her face as she first sees the finished hair
A few seconds of the finished hair moving
structure: Hard cut to the reaction (18s on)
talking: Just talk like you normally do. That's the point
Don't ask for a reaction. Let it happen
guide.caption: One line about this client and how long it had been.

Cutting: the big chop she trusted you with
